participant_roles: PresentationLayer=BookingRoute router + BookingController.bookDriver; ApplicationLayer=BookDriver use case (IBookDriverUseCase); DomainLayer=Booking entity + IBookingRepository/IDriverRepository ports; InfrastructureLayer=MongoBookingRepository/MongoDriverRepository + BookingModel
intent_and_evidence: Separates HTTP handling, business rules and persistence. The route only wires middleware to BookingController.bookDriver; the controller validates the DTO and calls _bookDriverUseCase.execute; BookDriver depends only on domain interfaces (IBookingRepository, IDriverRepository, INotificationService) and never on Express; the Mongo implementations live in infrastructure. Dependencies point inward except the noted AcceptBooking violation (see rejected/uncertain notes).

participant_roles: Injector/Container=tsyringe container; CompositionRoot=container.ts + useCaseContainer.ts + controllerContainer.ts; Tokens=TOKENS/USECASE_TOKENS symbols; Client=BookDriver (constructor @inject of 5 abstractions); Services=MongoBookingRepository, MongoDriverRepository, FareCalculatorService, SocketNotificationService, GoogleDistanceService; Resolver=BookingRoute (container.resolve)
intent_and_evidence: Objects do not construct their collaborators. container.ts binds each symbol token to an implementation (e.g. TOKENS.IBOOKING_REPO -> MongoBookingRepository, TOKENS.NOTIFICATION_SERVICE -> SocketNotificationService); BookDriver declares @inject(TOKENS.X) constructor parameters typed by interfaces; routes obtain fully wired controllers with container.resolve. index.ts imports the container modules before any route so registrations exist at resolve time.

participant_roles: Singleton=module-scoped variable io in socket.ts (no class; module plays the Singleton role); Initializer=initializeSocket(server); GlobalAccessPoint=getIO(); Clients=SocketNotificationService.io getter, NotificationSocket, index.ts
intent_and_evidence: Exactly one Socket.IO server must exist for the HTTP server. initializeSocket assigns the single module-level io once at start-up; every consumer obtains that same instance through getIO(), which throws if it is not initialised. SocketNotificationService uses a lazy getter so the instance is fetched only after initialisation. No class with a private constructor exists - the ES module cache provides the single instance.

participant_roles: Repository=IBookingRepository; LayerSupertype=IBaseRepository + BaseRepository<T,U>; ConcreteRepository=MongoBookingRepository; Entity=Booking; PersistenceModel=BookingModel; Clients=BookDriver, CancelBookingInputUseCase, UpdateBookingStatus, AttachPaymentIntentIdToBooking
intent_and_evidence: Trip use cases see a collection-like domain interface (createBooking, findBookingById, updateBooking, checkDriverAvailability) instead of Mongoose. MongoBookingRepository extends BaseRepository and maps calls onto BookingModel queries/aggregations; BookDriver and CancelBooking receive it through @inject(TOKENS.IBOOKING_REPO).

instance_name: Driver Repository with Geospatial Matching Query
participant_roles: Repository=IDriverRepository; LayerSupertype=BaseRepository<T,U>; ConcreteRepository=MongoDriverRepository; Entity=Driver; PersistenceModel=DriverModel (2dsphere index); Clients=BookDriver.findNearbyDriversWithinRadius, FindNearbyDrivers.findActiveDrivers, AdminChangeDriverStatus.updateStatus, CreatePaymentIntent.findDriverById
intent_and_evidence: Driver matching asks the repository for drivers within a radius; MongoDriverRepository hides the $geoNear aggregation (approved, unblocked, activePayment drivers) behind findNearbyDriversWithinRadius. Status changes go through updateStatus. Clients depend on the interface via @inject(TOKENS.IDRIVER_REPO).

participant_roles: Repository=IUserRepository; LayerSupertype=BaseRepository<T,U>; ConcreteRepository=MongoUserRepository; Entity=User; PersistenceModel=UserModel (userschema); Clients=FindNearbyDrivers (rider location), CheckBlockedUserOrDriver, AttachPaymentIntentIdToBooking
intent_and_evidence: Rider data (location used for matching, block flag used by middleware) is read through IUserRepository.getUserById; the Mongo implementation extends BaseRepository. Clients never touch UserModel directly.

participant_roles: Repository=IWalletRepository; LayerSupertype=BaseRepository<T,U>; ConcreteRepository=MongoWalletRepository; Entity=Wallet/WalletTransaction; PersistenceModel=WalletModel; Clients=AttachPaymentIntentIdToBooking (debit), WalletPayment.WalletRidePayment (debit), WalletService
intent_and_evidence: Ride payment use cases credit/debit the rider wallet through creditAmount/debitAmount on the interface; MongoWalletRepository keeps the transaction list consistent in MongoDB.

participant_roles: Repository=IDriverReviewRepository; LayerSupertype=BaseRepository<T,U>; ConcreteRepository=MongoDriverReviewRepository; Entity=DriverReview; PersistenceModel=ReviewModel; Clients=SubmitDriverReview, GetDriverReviews
intent_and_evidence: Driver ratings are stored and queried through IDriverReviewRepository (createReview, hasUserAlreadyReviewed, getReviewsByDriverId); the use cases rely only on that interface.

participant_roles: Mapper=DriverReviewMapper.toDomain / toPersistence (functions, no class); DomainObject=DriverReview; PersistenceRecord=ReviewDocument; Client=MongoDriverReviewRepository
intent_and_evidence: Keeps the domain object free of Mongoose types: toPersistence converts string ids to ObjectId before save and toDomain converts the stored document (and populated user) back to a plain DriverReview. The repository calls toPersistence before create and maps every query result with toDomain.

participant_roles: Target=INotificationService; Adapter=SocketNotificationService; Adaptee=Socket.IO Server (getIO) + Upstash Redis socket registry (redis.get driver:socket:<id>); Clients=BookDriver, AcceptBooking, CancelBookingInputUseCase, UpdateBookingStatus, AdminChangeDriverStatus, AttachPaymentIntentIdToBooking, CronScheduler
intent_and_evidence: Use cases speak a domain vocabulary (sendBookingNotification, cancelBookingNotification, paymentNotification...). SocketNotificationService translates each call into a Redis lookup of the recipient socket id followed by io.to(socketId).emit('<event>', data), so use cases never import Socket.IO or Redis.

participant_roles: Target=IStripeService; Adapter=PaymentService; Adaptee=Stripe SDK client (paymentIntents, transfers, balance); Clients=CreatePaymentIntent, AttachPaymentIntentIdToBooking, WalletPayment
intent_and_evidence: The domain-level interface expresses ride payments (createPaymentIntent with platformFee, transferToDriverFromWallet). PaymentService converts those calls into Stripe API calls (paymentIntents.create with application_fee_amount and transfer_data, transfers.create in paisa).

instance_name: Stripe Connect Driver Payout Onboarding Adapter
participant_roles: Target=IStripeAccountService; Adapter=StripeService (Accountservice.ts); Adaptee=module-level Stripe SDK client (accounts, accountLinks); Clients=OnboardDriverUseCase, VerifyDriverPaymentAccount
intent_and_evidence: Driver payout onboarding needs 'create account', 'create onboarding link' and 'retrieve account'. StripeService implements those three operations by calling stripe.accounts.create (express), stripe.accountLinks.create and stripe.accounts.retrieve.

participant_roles: Gateway=GoogleDistanceService.getDistances (concrete class, no interface); ExternalResource=Google Distance Matrix REST API via axios; Clients=BookDriver (road-distance filter <= 20 km), FindNearbyDrivers (sort by distance), NotificationSocket driver:online catch-up
intent_and_evidence: All road-distance lookups go through one object that builds the origins/destinations query, calls the API and returns a Record<driverOrBookingId, km>. Callers never see HTTP details. It is a Gateway rather than an Adapter because there is no separate target interface; clients inject the concrete class.

participant_roles: Subject=SocketNotificationService over the Socket.IO server (subject role combined, not separately declared); SubscriberRegistry=Redis keys driver:socket:<id>/user:socket:<id>; Subscribe=NotificationSocket driver:online/user:online handlers; Unsubscribe=disconnect handler; Notify=io.to(socketId).emit(event); ConcreteObservers=connected rider/driver Socket.IO clients (outside this repository)
intent_and_evidence: Riders and drivers register interest when their client emits driver:online/user:online (socket id stored in Redis) and are removed on disconnect. When a trip event happens (new booking, acceptance, cancellation, payment) the subject pushes it to every registered recipient with emit; broadcastBookingNotification loops over nearby driver ids and silently skips drivers with no socket. Publishers do not know how many observers exist.

participant_roles: Handler=Express middleware signature (req,res,next) (framework, not declared); ConcreteHandlers=protectRoute(roles) closure, CheckBlockedUserOrDriver.handle, catchAsync-wrapped BookingController handler, errorHandler; Client/ChainBuilder=BookingRoute, userRoutes and driverRoutes route definitions + app.use in index.ts
intent_and_evidence: Each handler either ends the request (401 no token, 403 wrong role, 403 blocked account) or calls next() to pass it on; errors thrown later travel to errorHandler, which picks the response by error type. The order is assembled per route, e.g. protectRoute(['user']) -> checkBlocked -> bookingController.bookDriver.

participant_roles: Component=Express RequestHandler interface; Decorator=catchAsync(fn) (higher-order function); ConcreteComponents=BookingController async handlers (bookDriver, cancelBooking, updateStatus...); Client=route definitions that register the wrapped handlers
intent_and_evidence: catchAsync returns a RequestHandler with the same (req,res,next) call shape as the wrapped controller function and adds one responsibility: a rejected promise is forwarded to next(err). Every BookingController action is declared as catchAsync(async ...), so error forwarding is added without modifying the handlers.
